title: Entertainment Update: Shania Twain Biopic Director, Horror Box Office Success, and Streaming News
text:
A roundup of major entertainment news including the Shania Twain biopic finding a director, A24's The Backrooms box office performance, Peacock's new action movie addition, Outlander prequel premiere date, Hulu renewals for The Testaments, new series details from The Handmaid's Tale producers, and MCU multiverse insights from Matt Shakman.
Sony Pictures' biopic of country music star Shania Twain has found its director, marking a significant step in the production of the much-anticipated life story.
The film will explore Twain's rise from humble beginnings in Canada to international superstardom, her musical evolution, and the personal and professional challenges she has overcome, including a highly publicized vocal cord diagnosis and a tumultuous marriage. Meanwhile, the upcoming Masters of the Universe film is generating buzz for featuring more post-credit scenes than typically expected, urging audiences to stay seated after the main feature.
In the horror genre, A24's adaptation of The Backrooms is rapidly becoming a box office phenomenon, captivating audiences with its unique viral horror premise. On the streaming front, Peacock has expanded its library with the addition of a major action movie starring Dwayne Johnson, John Cena, and Jason Momoa, a film that originally grossed over $714 million worldwide. STARZ celebrated World Outlander Day by announcing the premiere date for Season 2 of Outlander: Blood of My Blood, the prequel series.
Hulu has officially renewed The Testaments for a second season following strong viewership for its debut. The series, a sequel to The Handmaid's Tale, also saw the release of its official trailer, building anticipation for its launch.
Additionally, one of Hulu's highly anticipated shows, featuring breakout star Chase Infiniti from One Battle After Another, finally premiered. Regarding the Marvel Cinematic Universe, director Matt Shakman recently elaborated on the creative decision to set The Fantastic Four: First Steps on Earth-828 within the multiverse, linking it to the broader MCU narrative.
In television development, a new series from MGM and Scott Turow, executive produced by Marissa Jo Cerar, Bruce Miller, Priscilla Porianda through White Oak Pictures, and Matt Shakman, with 20th Television as the studio, is in the works. The show follows a private investigator named Pinky who is tasked with finding evidence to exonerate a female police chief accused of extorting sexual favors from male officers in exchange for promotions.
Cerar has a history with Miller from The Handmaid's Tale and has created and showrun Women of the Movement and Black Cake. Miller concluded The Handmaid's Tale after six seasons in 2025, earning 77 Emmy nominations and 15 wins, and quickly launched its sequel The Testaments, which earned a swift Season 2 renewal.
Shakman is an Emmy-nominated director for The Great and WandaVision and has directed episodes of Game of Thrones, The Boys, Succession, Billions, and It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia, in addition to his recent Marvel film. Vritti Johar is an Entertainment and Pop Culture writer at Evolve Media, covering a wide range of engaging content with a passion for cinema and storytelling, exploring art and photography in her free time
